Header.CaseTitle: R (Harrison) v Secretary of State for Justice

Counsel.Lead: Phillippa Kaufmann KC; Tom Hickman (instructed by Bhatt Murphy Solicitors)

SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Appellant seeks to establish that the withdrawal of library access and restrictions on distance learning materials constitute a breach of Article 2 Protocol 1 ECHR (right to education). The Administrative Court found unlawful administrative action but held the threshold for A2P1 violation was not met.

FactsReliedOn.item: The Appellant is serving a determinate sentence at HMP Wandsworth and is enrolled in an Open University degree program in Social Sciences.
In September 2024, following security concerns, the prison Governor implemented restrictions preventing prisoners from receiving printed course materials exceeding 50 pages per month.
The Appellant's OU course requires access to textbooks and journal articles totaling approximately 800 pages per semester.
Library access was reduced from 3 hours weekly to 1 hour fortnightly due to staffing shortages.
The Respondent acknowledged these restrictions were not in accordance with Prison Service Instructions but argued they did not meet the threshold for A2P1 interference.

Contentions.item: The Administrative Court applied an incorrect legal threshold for A2P1 violations, requiring near-complete denial of education rather than substantial interference with educational rights.
The Strasbourg jurisprudence establishes that A2P1 is violated where there is unjustified substantial interference with access to education, not only total denial.
The judge erred by refusing to consider events post-dating the claim form when assessing an ongoing violation brought by way of judicial review.
The cumulative effect of restricted library access and the 50-page limit rendered effective participation in higher education impossible.
Education is integral to rehabilitation purposes of imprisonment and restrictions must be justified as necessary and proportionate.

LegalBasis.item: Human Rights Act 1998, s.6 (acts of public authorities)
European Convention on Human Rights, Article 2 Protocol 1 (right to education)

ReliefSought.item: Declare that the restrictions constitute a violation of Article 2 Protocol 1 ECHR.
Quash the Governor's decision implementing the 50-page monthly limit.
Order the Respondent to ensure adequate library access and remove unreasonable restrictions on educational materials.

Timeline.Event: Appellant enrolled in Open University BA Social Sciences degree
Security incident at HMP Wandsworth leading to enhanced restrictions
Governor implements 50-page monthly limit on printed materials
Library access hours reduced from 3 hours weekly to 1 hour fortnightly
Appellant submits internal complaint regarding educational restrictions
Complaint rejected by Governor; adjudication confirms restrictions

SourceExtracts.Quote: The restrictions imposed prevent the Appellant from accessing the materials necessary to complete his degree course. An 800-page reading requirement cannot be satisfied with a 50-page monthly allowance.
Library access of one hour fortnightly is manifestly inadequate for a student pursuing higher education. The reduction from three hours weekly represents an 83% reduction in access.

While the Administrative Court found the Governor's decision unlawful under domestic administrative law, it held that the threshold for violation of Article 2 Protocol 1 had not been met. This sets an impermissibly high bar inconsistent with Strasbourg jurisprudence.

Education performs an integral role in rehabilitation. Restrictions that effectively prevent prisoners from completing higher education courses must be justified as necessary and proportionate, which these restrictions are not.

The jurisprudence of the European Court of Human Rights does not require complete denial of education before Article 2 Protocol 1 is engaged. Substantial and unjustified interference with access to education suffices.
